block_assessments.reasoning: Classical static regime and electrostatics correctly qualify the source topic; Coulomb1785 is supported by R3.
Cavendish/Maxwell and Cambridge manuscript account is expressly source-attributed, not asserted as verified priority or a newly established historical event.

Finite-body approximation requires separation large relative to size and nonzero dominant total charge. Residual shape/distribution effects are not said to vanish; neutral or distribution-dominated bodies are excluded from that simple approximation.

A given static distribution is divided into charge elements and combined by vector superposition; a conductor must first reach the appropriate equilibrium distribution. Scalar addition is not substituted for vector force.
Caption retains source1736-1806 and historical identity; electric, magnetic and friction research is not promoted into an invented priority claim.
Vacuum law is distinguished from an air approximation, which is explicitly conditional rather than a universal dielectric law.

B/A/a/c/b torsion apparatus description is complete. Small-force visibility depends on sensitivity and environment; fibre twist is a calibrated restoring torque, not an unconditional direct force reading.

Equal sharing is restricted to identical isolated conductors in symmetric surroundings after equilibrium; repeated initially neutral companion spheres yield halves and quarters. Source2/4 reduction is not described as amplification.
Coulomb magnitude law correctly specifies static point charges in vacuum and inverse-square separation.
Magnitude uses absolute charge amounts; separation is the positive point-charge distance.
Equation8-2 and all original math atoms remain unchanged; sign controls attraction/repulsion separately from the nonnegative magnitude interpretation.
Coefficient depends on the unit system; source unit-charge/unit-distance interpretation is correctly bounded to that chosen system.
Analogy with gravity is a similarity of mathematical form, not equality of mass/charge or a claim that electric interaction is always attractive.
Magnitude alone does not determine force direction.
Central attraction/repulsion and equal/opposite forces are restricted to the static situation. The forces act on different charges and cannot cancel as two forces on one body.
Coulomb interaction is a classical electrostatic characterization of charge, not a universal definition replacing the more general physical property.
